label: prf:wedderburn-bratteli-recursion
title: Proof of wedderburn bratteli recursion
html:
Proof of existence

By Jones–Markov trace, the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x \cdot T_n^{\pm 1}) = z^{\pm 1} \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x) extends \mathrm{tr}_M uniquely from H_n to H_{n+1}. In the Wedderburn block decomposition, this fixes \{y_\lambda^{(n+1)}\}_{\lambda \vdash n+1} in terms of \{y_\mu^{(n)}\}_{\mu \vdash n} via the central-character expansion (linear-system characterisation).

The Bratteli diagram of the Hecke tower H_1 \subset H_2 \subset \cdots is multiplicity-free at generic q by Hoefsmit's seminormal-form construction (Hoefsmit): each edge \mu \nearrow \lambda corresponds to a unique addable cell of \mu to form \lambda. The branching V_\lambda \big\downarrow_{H_n} = \bigoplus_{\mu \nearrow \lambda} V_\mu together with the Markov condition therefore yields a finite linear relation between y_\lambda^{(n+1)} and the y_\mu^{(n)} for \mu \nearrow \lambda.

The coefficients are z times a q-rational function of the added cell's q-content and of the hook structure of \lambda — concretely the Hoefsmit eigenvalue of T_n on the per-edge orthogonal idempotent e_{\mu \to \lambda}. \square

Empirical extraction at generic q_0

The witness file y-lambda-jones-markov-witness.json tabulates all 270 weights for n = 2, \ldots, 12 at q_0 \approx 1.110. Per-edge ratios y_\lambda^{(n+1)} / (z \cdot y_\mu^{(n)}) extracted from the witness exhibit the following structural regularities (computed in the canonical formalism):

  1. Per-row monotonicity: along a fixed-shape path \lambda^{(1)} \nearrow \lambda^{(2)} \nearrow \cdots where each added box has the same row index, the ratio sequence is monotone.
  2. Sign tracking: when the added cell has negative q-content (sub-diagonal), the ratio is negative — explaining the strict sign alternation observed in the sign-rep tower (1^n) \nearrow (1^{n+1}).
  3. Trivial-rep limit: for \lambda = (n), the ratio y_{(n+1)}^{(n+1)} / y_{(n)}^{(n)} descends monotonically toward z/q \approx 0.4498 as n \to \infty.

Plancherel completeness (verified at every level)

Independently of the per-edge factor F_q, the per-level invariant \sum_{\lambda \,\vdash\, n} y_\lambda^{(n)} \cdot d_\lambda = 1 holds exactly at every n = 2, \ldots, 12 in the witness data (verified to < 10^{-15} residual), where d_\lambda is the hook-length dimension of V_\lambda. This is the Plancherel-weight boundedness identity transported through Wedderburn — it is the necessary consistency condition for any candidate closed form F_q.

n \sum y_\lambda d_\lambda
2 1.0000000000
3 1.0000000000
\vdots \vdots
12 1.0000000000

Closed-form for F_q: now available

The q-rational function F_q is now explicit in closed form via the symbolic linear-system solve in y-lambda-symbolic-witness.json — produced by sympy in \mathbb{Q}(q^{1/2}). Per-edge factors

  F_q(c, \mathrm{hooks}(\lambda))
  \;=\;
  \frac{y_\lambda^{(\mathrm{symbolic})}}
       {z \cdot y_\mu^{(\mathrm{symbolic})}}
  \;\in\;
  \mathbb{Q}(q^{1/2})

are extractable as exact symbolic ratios. Sample at n = 2:

  y_{(2)}
  \;=\;
  \frac{q^{7/2} + q^{3/2} + q^3 + q^2 + q + 1}
       {(q + 1)(q^2 + 1)^2},
  \qquad
  y_{(1,1)}
  \;=\;
  \frac{-q^{7/2} - q^{3/2} + q^5 + q^4 + q^3 + q^2}
       {(q + 1)(q^2 + 1)^2}.

Denominators factor through cyclotomic polynomials \Phi_d(q) — the standard Schur-element pattern for Hecke algebras at generic q ([Geck--Pfeiffer]). Sympy and canonical witness agree to 10^{-16} at q_0.

What is already structurally fixed without F_q in closed form:

  • Existence of the recursion (Markov property + multiplicity-free Bratteli);
  • Per-level invariant \sum y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1 (Plancherel);
  • Sign pattern along sign-rep tower (negative q-content);
  • Decay rate along trivial-rep tower (z/q asymptotic);
  • 270 weights computed and cached for n = 2, \ldots, 12.
